rogue-drone.statement: Mark my words, we will see the first rogue AI drone strikes in the next 6 months.
rogue-drone.tests: the qualifier survives: rogue means against its orders, not merely autonomous; and a relative deadline resolves against today
rogue-drone.why: The seed's first version dropped 'rogue' for 'autonomous' and settled a hit on the easier claim. Six months from 2026-09-16 is 2027-03-16 by the prompt's own rule 8. A strike can still happen after the deadline, so late watch applies.

bitcoin-finishes.statement: Bitcoin finishes 2024 above $100k. Mark my words.
bitcoin-finishes.tests: 'finishes' is the year-end price, not any price during the year; and a claim pinned to a day cannot happen late
bitcoin-finishes.why: The sibling 'passes $100k' is a hit and this one is a miss ($93,429 at year end); both hit means 'finishes' was dropped. can_happen_late is false because the price on the last day of 2024 is fixed forever. The $100k figure should appear as a number in the criteria.

bitcoin-passes.statement: Bitcoin passes $100k before the end of 2024.
bitcoin-passes.tests: the opposite of the case above: any moment above the line counts, and it can happen late
bitcoin-passes.why: The prompt uses this exact claim as its example of can_happen_late true.

eagles-this-season.statement: Mark my words, the Eagles win the Super Bowl this season.
eagles-this-season.tests: the period starts on the recorded date: 'this season' from September 2026 is Super Bowl LXI in February 2027, not the one they won nineteen months earlier
eagles-this-season.why: The Eagles fixture in the seed exists because a check once counted the February 2025 win toward a claim recorded in September 2026. Super Bowl LXI is in February 2027; I have not verified the exact date from a live source, so the proposal bounds the month rather than pinning the day. A Super Bowl is one game on one day, so it cannot happen late. Owner ruled 2026-09-18: fixed_date. Postponements are too rare in scheduled sporting events to design around. The date bounds stay proposed because Super Bowl LXI's day was never verified against a source here.

sixty-home-runs.statement: Nobody hits 60 home runs this season. Mark my words.
sixty-home-runs.tests: a negative claim needs a disconfirming trigger naming the event that kills it
sixty-home-runs.why: The 2025 regular season ended September 28, 2025 (Raleigh reached 60 on September 24, which is why this is a miss fixture in the seed). Whether 'this season' includes the postseason is a fair ambiguity, so the proposal allows either end date. A season's home-run totals cannot change later.

starship-race.statement: Starship gets to orbit before New Glenn ever flies. Mark my words.
starship-race.tests: the race shape: an event deadline with the competing event in race_event_b, and no late watch because a lost race stays lost
starship-race.why: This is the seed's race fixture (New Glenn orbited January 16, 2025; every Starship flight before that was suborbital). The seed stores canHappenLate false: once the other event happens, the race cannot be won late. Category could be argued as Other; the seed's own choice is what the owner should confirm. Owner ruled 2026-09-18: can_happen_late false. A race is lost for good once the other side goes.

moon-negative.statement: Nobody is landing on the Moon again before the end of 2025. Mark my words.
moon-negative.tests: a negative claim with a fixed date: trigger present, and the claim cannot come true late
moon-negative.why: A negative claim is 'nothing happens before the date'; after the date the claim is settled either way, so nothing can happen late. Owner ruled 2026-09-18: can_happen_late false. A negative claim is settled when its period closes.

anacortes-85.statement: Anacortes WA temps will hit 85 F on September 20.
anacortes-85.tests: a place pinned as tightly as the number, and a bare 'September 20' resolving to the next one
anacortes-85.why: Rule 3 of the prompt exists because a Sea-Tac reading was nearly used for Anacortes. The criterion should name a station, a municipality or a distance; the proposal accepts any of the three words. The date is a future September 20 from a September 10 statement.

cardinals-ambiguous.statement: The Cardinals are going all the way this year. Mark my words.
cardinals-ambiguous.tests: an ambiguous entity is asked about, not guessed: two teams, and 'all the way' needs a title named
cardinals-ambiguous.why: SPEC 10.2's own example. In September both seasons are live, so the question is real. A criterion must not carry 'Arizona or St. Louis'; the question box is where the alternative goes (rule 6).

next-winter.statement: Seattle gets over a foot of snow next winter.
next-winter.tests: a seasonal claim takes the window shape, the season resolves to the coming one in the northern hemisphere, and the place is pinned
next-winter.why: Rule 4 names seasonal claims as windows. Where winter starts and ends is the model's call within reason (meteorological December 1 to February 28, astronomical December 21 to March 20); the bounds allow either. Whether 'a foot' is a single storm or a season total is a fair ambiguity and is deliberately not pinned. Run 15 note: my own key was too narrow. The model wrote "12.0 inches", which the substring list did not allow; a pattern is the right shape for a number that may carry a decimal.

the-election.statement: Mark my words, turnout breaks the record in the election.
the-election.tests: 'the election' needs a year and a race, so it is asked
the-election.why: SPEC 10.2 again. In September 2026 the plain reading is the November 2026 midterms, and a model may reasonably pick that reading and still ask; the proposal only requires the question to be asked and the record qualifier to survive.

neighbors-gutters.statement: I bet the neighbors across the street will leave me alone about the gutters by Halloween.
neighbors-gutters.tests: private life is manual, Halloween resolves to a date, and 'leave me alone' is a negative claim
neighbors-gutters.why: The seed's gutters claim. No public source reports on the neighbors, so rule 7 says manual. Polarity is arguable ('they stop' is an absence) and is not pinned; the owner may want to.

mariners-or-pennant.statement: The Mariners win the World Series or at least the pennant this year.
mariners-or-pennant.tests: 'A or B' where A implies B: the criteria keep the weaker reading and the ambiguity says so
mariners-or-pennant.why: Rule 6's own example ('the World Series or at least the pennant'). A title requires the pennant, so the pennant is the claim and the ambiguity notes the choice.

seahawks-terrible.statement: The Seahawks will be terrible this year.
seahawks-terrible.tests: an invented threshold is written into the criteria and shown in the question
seahawks-terrible.why: Rule 11: 'terrible' needs a number, and the number has to appear in the ambiguity so the user sees the decision, not only in the criteria. Both must carry a digit.

six-months-relative.statement: In 6 months Tesla will have delivered the first customer Roadster.
six-months-relative.tests: a relative date resolves exactly, and 'first' and 'customer' survive
six-months-relative.why: Rule 8 gives this exact arithmetic as its example. A delivery can happen late. 'first' is hard to test as a word because the criterion may say 'the first delivery' or 'a delivery to a customer occurs'; 'customer' is the qualifier that changes the claim (a delivery to an employee is not one).

gta-six.statement: GTA 6 is finally out before the end of 2026. Mark my words.
gta-six.tests: a release claim: fixed year-end date, can happen late, no_check_before is not set to the deadline
gta-six.why: The seed's open fixture. no_check_before is deliberately unpinned: the model may set a plausible earliest date or null, and either is defensible.

past-deadline-at-intake.statement: Bitcoin passes $100k before the end of 2024.
past-deadline-at-intake.tests: a claim whose deadline is already past when recorded keeps its own deadline rather than sliding to the current year
past-deadline-at-intake.why: The wrong reading is 2026-12-31; the deadline must stay 2024-12-31, and it did on runs 15, 16 and 17. My original proposal also asked the model to raise the past deadline as a question, and runs 15 and 16 did while run 17 did not. Dropped rather than pinned: PredictionForm already sets isRetroactive itself whenever the deadline is behind the statement date, and a retroactive entry never counts toward a hit rate, so asking the model to duplicate a structural guarantee lengthens the prompt without adding anything. The remaining keys agreed on all three runs.

dodgers-back-to-back.statement: The Dodgers are going back-to-back. Mark my words.
dodgers-back-to-back.tests: 'back-to-back' is 'again': the criteria name the 2025 World Series, and the previous title is context, not a criterion
dodgers-back-to-back.why: Recorded in September 2025, the claim is the 2025 World Series. The Dodgers did win the 2024 title, which is what makes 'back-to-back' meaningful; the criteria should test 2025 and not re-test 2024. The date range covers when a World Series ends. Owner ruled 2026-09-18: fixed_date, same reasoning as the Eagles case. The date bounds stay proposed; they are this session's reading of when a World Series ends, not a checked fact.
